title: Power System: Battery, BMS and Power Distribution

blocks.text: This chapter describes the electrical energy system of the digital twin: the 48 V LiFePO4 traction pack, the BMS ECU firmware model, the power distribution unit (PDU) and low-voltage rails, the hard-wired safety chain, the implement drives and the dock charger. For each part it states what is modelled, which file and parameters implement it, how it behaves in the Phase 1 demonstration and where the model deviates from its specification. All parameters are in `params/param_power.m` and appear as `P.power` after project startup. The design source is `docs/specs/power.md` (revision B), together with decisions D30 (safety-chain re-arm), D45 (hot charging), D46 (shift budget) and D48 (end-of-life estimation) in `docs/architecture.md`.
Power domain at a glance

The power domain has two parts. The **physical plant** is the Subsystem Reference `subsystems/power/Power_Plant.slx`, block `Power` inside the Model block `Shaddad_Plant`. It contains Simscape Electrical, Simscape Battery and thermal networks plus 1 ms discrete logic for relays and the safety chain. The **BMS firmware** is the separate model `models/Shaddad_BMS.slx`, Model block `BMS` in `Shaddad_System`, beside the plant. The plant sends the measurement bus `Bus_BMS_Meas` to the BMS every 10 ms and receives `Bus_BMS_Cmd` (contactor, balancing, fan and charger commands) through a Unit Delay that breaks the algebraic loop. The MCU never touches the contactors directly. It talks to the BMS only over CAN1 (request frame 0x3D0 in, seven telemetry frames out), and it acts on the hardware through three digital outputs into the safety chain.

blocks.text: Battery pack
Cell model

Every cell is the Simscape Battery block `Battery Equivalent Circuit` with one RC pair and a lumped thermal mass. Current dependence, hysteresis, self-discharge and cycling ageing are disabled. All parameters are 2-D tables over 12 SOC breakpoints and four temperatures (0, 25, 45 and 60 °C):

OCV(SOC,T) = OCV25(SOC) + kT(SOC)*(T - 298.15)
R0(SOC,T)  = R0_25(SOC) * fR0(T)        R1(SOC,T) = R1_25(SOC) * fR1(T)
tau1(T)    = 40 s * ftau(T)
v_term     = OCV - i*R0 - v1            dv1/dt = -v1/tau1 + i/C1,  C1 = tau1/R1
m*cp*dT/dt = i^2*R0 + v1^2/R1 - (T - T_air)/R_amb_cell      (R_amb_cell = 4.0 K/W)

At 25 °C the rest OCV runs from 2.73 V at 0 % SOC over a flat 3.27-3.33 V plateau (35-90 % SOC) to 3.60 V at 100 %. R0 is 0.78-1.40 mΩ per cell and rises by a factor of 2.2 at 0 °C. Two values deviate from the spec table on purpose (T04): OCV(0) = 2.73 V, so that the 2.5 V cut-off falls exactly at SOC 0, and an end-of-charge knee (3.40 V at 98 %), without which the cell never reaches the 3.55 V CV level and charging never ends.
Pack assembly with the Battery Builder

`build_shaddad_battery` assembles the pack programmatically (`batteryCell` -> `batteryParallelAssembly(cell, 3)` -> `batteryModule(pa, 16)` -> `buildBattery`) and writes the libraries `Shaddad_Battery_lib.slx` and `Shaddad_Battery_Lumped_lib.slx`. The SSRs `Pack_Grouped16` and `Pack_Lumped` place the generated block and set every mask value to a `P.power.*` expression; the generated `*_param.m` scripts are reference only. Both variants have the same ports: `pack_p`/`pack_n`, thermal `AmbH`, input `Bal_Cmd[16]` and the truth outputs `SOC_true`, `V_cell_true`, `T_cell_true` (16 values each, from a Simscape Probe). {tab:tab_pwr_packvar} compares the two pack variants, and {fig:F10_battery_pack.png} shows the generated module inside `Pack_Grouped16`.

blocks.text: Ageing is a parameter, not a state: `P.power.pack.age.cap_factor` and `P.power.pack.age.R0_factor` scale capacity and R0 (1 = new). The end-of-life benches use 0.8 and 1.5.
Pack thermal network

`Pack_Thermal` connects the 16 cell-group masses (2178 J/K per cell) through the module ambient path to an AIR node (8 kg x 900 J/(kg K)), which exchanges heat with a steel WALL node (15 kg x 480 J/(kg K)) and with the outside air:

items: AIR-WALL natural convection 4.8 W/K; WALL-ambient convection 14 W/K plus radiation (emissivity 0.85, 1.4 m²)
Solar heat into the wall: 0.6 x 0.25 m² x G_solar, with G_solar and the ambient temperature from `Bus_EnvState`
Two 12 W fans: variable convection AIR-ambient with h = 20 W/(m² K) x Fan_Cmd x `k_filter` (`k_filter` = 0.5 models a clogged dust filter); their 24 W load is on the 24 V rail
While docked (D45) the fan inlet takes conditioned dock air at 30 °C and the fans are forced on

blocks.text: The cell-mass time constant is about 3 h, so pack temperature carries over from one shift to the next. Short Phase 1 runs therefore show almost no temperature change.
BMS ECU model (Shaddad_BMS)

`Shaddad_BMS` is the firmware model of a dedicated STM32G4 BMS board (configuration set `cs_STM32G4`, CubeMX project `utilities/stm32/shaddad_g474.ioc`). It is single precision and fixed-step discrete with a 10 ms base rate. The top level is `IO_In` -> `BMS_Core` (atomic) -> `BMS_CAN_Pack` -> `IO_Out`. `IO_In` and `IO_Out` are Variant Subsystems on `VC_TARGET`: 0 is a SIM pass-through, 1 uses `stm32blockslib` blocks (SPI for the cell-monitor AFE, ADC, GPIO contactor drivers, FDCAN1). Most algorithms are Simscape Battery BMS library blocks (`batt_sl_lib`). Stateflow is not installed (D1), so the contactor state machine is a MATLAB Function block whose body is `subsystems/power/bms_mode_manager.m`. {fig:F14_bms_top.png} shows the top level of `Shaddad_BMS`, and {tab:tab_pwr_bmscore} lists the units inside `BMS_Core`.

blocks.text: **Current sign.** The Shaddad buses use + = discharge. The `batt_sl_lib` blocks use + = charge, so `Meas` feeds them with -I_pack, and the library limits in `P.power.bms.pwr_est` are given as [-discharge, +charge]. Keep this in mind when you probe signals inside `BMS_Core`.
Protection and fault reporting
{tab:tab_pwr_prot} lists the BMS protections with their parameters in `P.power.bms` and the bits they set in `Fault_Word` and `Warning_Word`.

blocks.caption: BMS protections (P.power.bms) and their Fault_Word / Warning_Word bits
rows: sum of cells vs pack voltage, 1.0 V

blocks.text: Critical bits (0-5, 8, 14, 15) drive the mode manager into FAULT, which opens all contactors. Latched bits clear only on a rising edge of `Fault_Reset_Req` once the symptom is gone. `Fault_Level` summarises the word: 3 = HV off (bits 0-8, 14, 15), 2 = derate (bits 9-13, 17-20), 1 = warning or safety relay open (b16, so every E-stop shows Fault_Level 1 at the BMS).The MCU reacts with a controlled stop (class B) to BMS_TIMEOUT (bit 9, any BMS frame older than 0.5 s), BMS_ALARM (bit 10, Fault_Level 3), HV_LOST (bit 17) and HV_OPENING (bit 18), and derates to 50 % on BMS_WARN (bit 11, warning word not zero or DCL below 50 A).
Contactor and precharge mode manager

`BMS_ModeManager` runs every 10 ms and implements the transition table of spec section 4.1 in priority order. The `after(t)` timers of the original Stateflow design are tick counters in the current state. The state code is reported as `Contactor_State` (enumeration `BmsContactorState`). The chart uses `Safety_HV_OK`, the coil supply of K1/K2 through the delayed safety-relay contacts, as its safety input. {tab:tab_pwr_fsm} lists the contactor states.

blocks.caption: BMS contactor states (bms_mode_manager.m, parameters P.power.bms.chart)
rows: critical fault -> FAULT; HV_Enable_Req and Safety_HV_OK and not docked and armed -> PRECHARGE; docked and Charge_Enable_Req -> CHARGING
request or Safety_HV_OK lost -> STANDBY; at least 0.25 s and V_bus ≥ 0.97 V_pack -> CLOSE_MAIN; 1.5 s -> PRE_FAIL
Safety_HV_OK lost -> STANDBY (hardware already opened K1); fault, request off or Shutdown_Req -> OPENING
abs(I_pack) < 10 A or 0.2 s -> WELD_CHECK (MCU ramps torque to zero)
after 5 s: V_bus > 0.95 V_pack -> FAULT (weld, b7), else STANDBY
third failure -> FAULT (b6); otherwise retry after 5 s -> STANDBY
critical fault -> FAULT; undocked or request off -> STANDBY; charge complete -> CHARGE_DONE
rising Fault_Reset_Req with no critical fault -> STANDBY

blocks.text: An internal *armed* latch prevents an automatic HV restart. After a `Safety_HV_OK` drop or a completed opening, the BMS re-enters PRECHARGE only after `HV_Enable_Req` has fallen and risen again. The MCU produces this edge when the operator resets and re-arms.
SOC, SOE, SOH and runtime estimation

items: **SOC per group:** `SOC Estimator (Kalman Filter, Variable Capacity)` for all 16 groups (extended Kalman filter, state [SOC; v1], group tables 300 Ah and R/3, Q = diag(1e-7, 1e-6), R = 1e-4 V²). The high R makes the filter coulomb-count on the flat LFP plateau and correct at the knees. The cell voltages are first corrected by an R0 ageing ratio learned at current steps of at least 10 A.

**Pack SOC (display):** SOC_pack = SOC_min / (1 - (SOC_max - SOC_min)), limited to [0, 1]: 0 when the weakest group is empty, 1 when the strongest is full. A coulomb-counting estimator runs in parallel as plausibility check (`SOC_cc`).

**Capacity, SOH, SOE:** least-squares capacity estimator (1 s, rate limit 1e-3 Ah/s, bounds 200-310 Ah); SOH = (Ah - 240) / (300 - 240), so 1 = new and 0 = end of life; energy-counting SOE with capacity Ah x 51.2 V.

**Runtime and power capability:** E_remaining = Ah x 51.2 V x max(SOC_pack - 0.10, 0); Runtime_Remaining_s = 3600 E_remaining / max(P_avg, 200 W), with P_avg the 600 s moving average of pack power (used by the Phase 2 GNC for return-to-dock). The Battery Power Estimator gives the 10 s capability `P_dis_lim_W` / `P_chg_lim_W`.

blocks.text: Current limits, charge control, balancing and fans

items: **Discharge limit (E13):** temperature tables for the coolest and the hottest cell plus a voltage-headroom term (R0 = 0.4 mΩ). Coolest cell: 60 A at -20 °C, 150 A at 0 °C, 300 A from 10 °C. Hottest cell: 300 A up to 45 °C, then 250 / 150 / 0 A at 50 / 55 / 60 °C. A SOC taper multiplies the limit by 0.5 below 10 % and by 0.2 below 5 % (on SOC_min).
**Charge limit (E14, D45 table):** 0 A at 0 °C, 15 A at 5 °C, 30 A at 10 °C, 100 A from 15 °C to 50 °C, 50 A at 55 °C, 0 A at 60 °C.

**CC-CV (E15):** PI loop on V_max, CV at 3.55 V per group (Kp 2000, Ki 400, re-tuned in T04). Request = min(CC-CV, I_chg_lim, 100 A), only while CHARGING; complete when V_max ≥ 3.545 V and I < 10 A for 60 s; voltage request (CVL) 56.8 V.
**Balancing (E16):** passive, 10 mV threshold, 3 mV hysteresis, 1 s rate, only while CHARGING or at rest (abs(I) < 2 A) and V_max > 3.40 V, because LFP imbalance is observable only at the top knee.
**Fans (E17):** ON 40 °C / OFF 35 °C on the hottest cell, only if the cells are hotter than the outside air minus 1 K, forced on above 50 °C.

blocks.text: CAN interface

CAN1 is classic CAN 2.0B at 500 kbit/s with 11-bit IDs and little-endian payloads. The codecs `bmsreq_can_pack/unpack` and `bms_can_pack/unpack` (Byte Pack / Byte Unpack with scaling) are the same files on the BMS and the MCU side. {tab:tab_pwr_can} lists the BMS frames.

blocks.text: **Code generation is blocked.** Building `Shaddad_BMS` for the STM32G4 needs Simulink Coder, which is licensed but not installed on this PC. The HW variant (`VC_TARGET = 1`) updates without errors after the fix pass of 2026-10-23 (BMS FDCAN Read/DI port order), but no target code has been generated or measured yet.
Power distribution
PDU single-line

PACK+ --R_cab 0.34 mOhm--F_MAIN 300 A--+ BATT+
  BATT+ --K2 precharge--R_pre-------------+
  BATT+ --K1 main 300 A-------------------+-- DCBUS+ --+--F_TL 150 A--0.98 mOhm-- DC48_TracL (left ESC)
                                                      +--F_TR 150 A--0.98 mOhm-- DC48_TracR (right ESC)
                                                      +--F_IMP 100 A---------- IMP48 (mower / tiller drive)
                                                      +--C_PDU 100 uF, ESR 5 mOhm, bleed 5 kOhm
  BATT+ --S_KEY--F_AUX 30 A-- AUX48 --> LV_Distribution (DC-DC 24 V and 12 V)
  BATT+ --K4 charge--F_CHG 125 A-- DOCK+ --> Dock_Charger
  BATT+ --BMS supply 2 W
PACK- --R_SHUNT 100 uOhm-- GND   (only Electrical Reference of the 48 V network)

AUX48 is tapped after the main fuse and the key switch but before K1. The LV rails, and with them the MCU and the sensors, therefore stay powered when an E-stop opens K1. The BMS is fed directly from BATT+ (2 W constant-power load) and stays powered even with the key off. Only the key switch removes LV power. The Electrical Reference sits after the shunt, so no return current can bypass the current measurement. The single Solver Configuration of the network is at the `Shaddad_Plant` top level on `DC48_TracL_n` (D15).

blocks.text: The On-Off Delay in each coil path models pickup and dropout. Its output also serves as the auxiliary contact (`K_fb` to the BMS, DI b6/b7 to the MCU). Each fuse reports its blown state into the `Fuse_Blown` bit word for the BMS and the MCU.
Precharge

The spec assumes 5.5 mF of total bus capacitance (2 x 2.2 mF ESC DC links, 1 mF implement drive, 0.1 mF PDU). With R_pre = 22 Ω this gives τ = 0.121 s, 97 % in 0.42 s, a 2.4 A peak and 7.8 J per precharge. Bench test T-PWR-03 (`tests/power/t_power_plant.m`) confirms 0.42 ± 0.05 s and an inrush I²t below 2 A²s when K1 closes. In the integrated system, however, the two ESCs draw about 2 x 7 W of idle power from the DC link. With 22 Ω this holds V_bus at 87 % of V_pack, below the 97 % close threshold, so precharge times out and HV_Ready never rises. All system scenarios therefore apply the integration override `P.sim.ovr.R_pre = 4.7` through `utilities/scn_integration_overrides.m`. The final value is still open (see {tab:tab_pwr_dev}).

blocks.text: The converters are the averaged `ee_lib` DC-DC Converter (no switching ripple; losses = fixed loss of 4 / 3 / 0.3 W plus a term proportional to I², fitted to `eff_rated` at `P_rated`). The loads are Dynamic Load blocks driven by the power demands of `Bus_LV_LoadDemand` from the electronics plant; demands in W rather than A cannot form algebraic loops. `Rail_*_OK` flags mark rails within ±10 %, and the MCU raises RAIL_UV (bit 19) when V24 < 21.6 V, V12 < 11.0 V or V5 < 4.6 V.
Power sensing and energy audit
`Power_Sensors` turns plant quantities into three buses:

items: `Bus_BMS_Meas` (10 ms), what the BMS sees: cell voltages (σ 1 mV, ±2 mV offset), shunt current (σ 0.05 A, 0.10 A offset, 0.3 % gain error), pack, bus and dock voltages (σ 20 mV), NTC temperatures (σ 0.3 K, 5 s lag), plus contactor, dock, key, safety and fuse states, all with seeded noise.
`Bus_PowerStatus` (1 ms): true rail voltages and currents, rail-OK flags, K3, Safety_OK, Safety_HV_OK, E-stop status and fuse word for the MCU hardware front end.

`Bus_PowerTruth` (100 ms, integrals at 1 ms): true SOC, voltage and temperature per group, pack current and the energies E_out, E_in, E_trac_dc, E_impl_dc, E_lv, E_dcdc_loss, E_pdu_loss and E_chg_bus. `Sim_Monitors` closes the electrical energy audit eps_el (D40) from them; in S1 the residual is 6.1e-14.

blocks.text: Hard-wired safety chain

`Safety_Chain` models the hard-wired E-stop loop and the safety relay as discrete 1 ms logic. Its central rule (D30) is that the MCU can **open** the loop through its watchdog-relay output DO0 but can **never close** it. Closing always needs a reset edge while the loop is healthy. {fig:F11_safety_chain.png} shows `Power_Plant/Safety_Chain`; the logic is summarised below.

blocks.caption: Power_Plant/Safety_Chain: loop AND of the E-stop, bumper, wireless, MCU and key inputs; stretched reset edge; reset-dominant SR latch; immediate (Safety_OK) and delayed (Safety_HV_OK) contacts; coil gating of K1-K4.

blocks.text:
Loop_OK      = NOT(estop_front OR estop_rear OR wireless_estop_tripped OR bumper_front OR bumper_rear)
               AND MCU_Safety_OK (DO0) AND key_on
Reset_pulse  = On-Off Delay( rising(reset_btn OR Safety_Reset_Req DO1), Td_on 0, Td_off 50 ms )
Armed        = SR latch( Set = Loop_OK AND Reset_pulse, Reset = NOT Loop_OK ), reset dominant
Safety_OK    = On-Off Delay(Armed, on 20 ms, off 15 ms)   -> ESC STO (both sides), implement ECU, K3
Safety_HV_OK = On-Off Delay(Armed, on 20 ms, off 1.5 s)   -> K1/K2 coil supply (stop category 1)
K1_coil = K1_Cmd AND Safety_HV_OK          K2_coil = K2_Cmd AND Safety_HV_OK
K3_coil = ImpPwr24_Enable (DO2) AND Safety_OK
K4_coil = K4_Cmd AND dock_contact          (charging stays possible with an E-stop pressed)
EStop_Ch1_OK = NOR(front, rear)            EStop_Ch2_OK = Ch1 OR estop_ch2_stuck (fault injection)
{tab:tab_pwr_safety} lists the safety-chain signals between the MCU, the plant and the drives.

blocks.caption: Safety-chain signals between MCU, plant and drives
rows: Watchdog relay: watchdog healthy AND no MCU-internal fault (maskDO0 = bits 5-8, 23, 25) AND mode not BOOT
50 ms pulse, once at SELFTEST entry and on every reset request (button or RC CH9), issued 20 ms after DO0 is high
Immediate contacts -> ESC STO, implement ECU, K3, MCU DI b2
Torque off 15 ms after a trip
Delayed contacts -> K1/K2 coils, BMS, MCU DI b12
HV removed 1.5 s after a trip
HW_ESTOP (bit 0); SAFETY_CHAIN_DISCREPANCY (bit 27) if the channels disagree for 0.05 s

blocks.text: Stop category 1 gives the ESCs 1.5 s to brake the robot (2 m/s at 2 m/s² takes 1.0 s) and the implement drives time to brake their blades before HV is removed. Setting `P.power.safety.t_cat1 = 0` turns the chain into category 0. MCU class-A bits 0, 27, 29 and 31 are consequences of the hardware chain: they stop the robot, but they are excluded from DO0, otherwise the loop could never re-close.

**Measured behaviour.** In S8a (front E-stop at 1.19 m/s) STO acts 15 ms after the plant-side button edge (limit 20 ms), and the MCU sets HW_ESTOP 8 ms after it sees the DI change (limit 11 ms). The robot stops within 0.213 m (limit 0.6 m) and creeps at most 0.0007 m/s while stopped. It resumes to 1.19 m/s after reset and re-arm. Bench T-PWR-04 confirms Safety_OK low within 20 ms, K3 open within 30 ms and K1 open at 1.5 ± 0.03 s. Releasing the button does not re-close anything, and HV_Ready returns within 1.0 s after a reset and a new HV_Enable_Req edge.

The remote E-stop on RC channel 12 is a software stop. The MCU enters ESTOP, but the stop is not safety rated and does not open this hardware loop. Only the front and rear E-stop buttons, the bumpers, the wireless E-stop input, the MCU watchdog relay and the key switch open the loop.

24 V PM DC pump motor (3000 rpm) behind an averaged buck; 8 nozzle solenoids x 8 W
Pump duty with soft start 1.5 1/s; ready at 80 % of set pressure

blocks.text: The 48 V drives have a DC-voltage-dependent torque envelope (zero torque at V_dc ≤ 30 V), so a dead bus with K1 open never demands infinite current, and a 60 V clamp limits regenerative pumping of an isolated DC link. Standby and iron losses are not modelled. The deck lift (150 W) loads V24_IMP. The load mechanics (blade windage and cutting, soil torque, pump) belong to the structure plant on `Impl_Shaft`; one variable `VC_IMPL` selects drive and load together.

`impl_ecu` models the commercial implement drive controller at 10 ms. It decodes IMPL_CMD (0x140, 50 ms, speed at blade or rotor), forces the reference to zero on a 0.2 s CAN timeout, when disabled or when Safety_OK is low, ramps it, runs the PI speed loop (output: torque reference) and returns IMPL_FB (0x141) with running/fault/ready status, implement type, speed, current, temperature and an alive counter. The detailed fault code (OC, OV, UV, OT, CAN_TIMEOUT, STALL, SAFETY_OFF) is in `Bus_ImplElecState.Fault_Code`. In Phase 1 the operator switches the implement with RC channel 8 (OFF / ON / ON + auto-spray). The default demo runs with `VC_IMPL = 0`; `phase1_test_drive(..., 'Implement', 1)` loads the mower.
Dock charger

items: **VC_CHG = 1 (default), BMS-controlled:** controlled current source I = dock x Charger_Enable x min(I_req, 100 A, 5.5 kW / V_dock), slew-limited to 20 A/s with a 0.5 s lag. It has hardware OVP at 58.4 V, an output diode (no back-feed, no inrush when K4 closes), a 10 kΩ bleed and 15 mΩ dock contacts. Grid power = V x I / 0.94.
**VC_CHG = 2:** the `batt_lib/Cyclers/Charger` block (90 A, CV 56.8 V, cut-off 10 A) for pack tests without the BMS.

**Sequence:** dock contact and Charge_Enable_Req -> BMS CHARGING -> K4 closes -> charger enabled after 0.1 s -> CC at min(100 A, I_chg_lim) -> CV at 3.55 V per group -> complete after 60 s below 10 A -> CHARGE_DONE (K4 opens).
**Hot climate (D45):** while docked the fans are forced on with 30 °C conditioned air. Bench T-PWR-10b requires 0.10 -> 0.95 SOC within 3.6 h with cells at or below 45 °C at 50 °C ambient.

blocks.text: Charging is not part of the Phase 1 demonstration. It is verified on the power benches: `tests/power/tb_pack_bms.slx` (charge, hot charge, balancing) and `tb_shift_cycle.slx` (24 h shift cycle T-PWR-20, at least three shifts per day at 45 °C and 50 °C, both passing in `t_power_plant`).
Power-up sequence

The power-up and re-arm sequence is normative (ICD section 6, D30). The S0 scenario checks it: `run_scenario('S0')` simulates it, and the System regression `tests/system/tScenarios.m` (tags System and Long, not part of `run_regression('Fast')`) evaluates the latest saved S0 result.

items: t = 0: the MCU is in BOOT with DO0 = 0. The safety relay is open, because the reset-dominant latch sees Loop_OK = 0.
BOOT -> SELFTEST after one tick. DO0 (MCU_SAFETY_OK) rises as soon as the watchdog ages are healthy: **0.02 s**.
20 ms later the MCU emits the automatic DO1 re-arm pulse (**50 ms**). `Safety_Chain` stretches the reset edge to 50 ms, so Set = Loop_OK AND Reset_pulse closes the relay.
After the 20 ms contact pickup, Safety_OK and Safety_HV_OK rise: **0.061 s**.

The MCU sends HV_Enable_Req in BMS_REQ (key on, no class-A fault, mode not BOOT or FAULT). The BMS precharges (K2, at least 0.25 s, V_bus ≥ 0.97 V_pack), closes K1, opens K2 after 50 ms and reports HV_Ready: **0.5 s**.
SELFTEST -> STANDBY at `selftest_t` = 1.0 s, once rails, drives, BMS and IMU report fresh data: **1.01 s**.
The operator arms (CH6, sticks neutral) and selects MANUAL (CH5). In the D1 demo MANUAL starts at 2.04 s.

blocks.text: If an E-stop is pressed at power-up, the relay stays open, HW_ESTOP latches and the MCU enters ESTOP. Releasing the button and pressing reset (or RC CH9) makes the MCU clear the latch and issue a new DO1 pulse. The relay closes, the MCU returns to STANDBY, and a new arm edge is needed before the robot moves.

**Measured sequence.** The S0 power-up smoke test (`scn_S0_smoke.m`, 10 s, Normal mode) was re-run on 2026-10-23 at 20:47 (`work/results/S0_20261023_204711.mat`) and passes all 11 criteria with the times given in the list above, a position drift of 0 m and an SOC change of 1.6e-5. {tab:tab_s0_crit} lists the criteria and {fig:F25_s0_powerup.png} shows the timeline ({sec:ch09_results/Power-up and safety re-arm (S0)}).
Energy budget

The pack is sized for the 4 h design shift of D46: 70 % cutting at the site working speed and 30 % transit, turns and idle with the implement off, on the worst site (palm farm, farm soil, mower configuration). Usable energy per shift = E_nom x (SOC0 0.95 - return-to-home threshold 0.215) x SOH x 0.97 discharge efficiency = **10.95 kWh new** and **8.76 kWh at end of life** (SOH 0.8). The values are in `P.power.budget`. {tab:tab_pwr_budget} gives the budget for three working speeds.

blocks.caption: Shift power budget, revision B (docs/specs/power.md 2.1, D46)

blocks.text: The palm-row working speed `P.gnc.spd.v_work_palm` is therefore 1.0 m/s, and the GNC limits speed in dense vegetation. Continuous cutting at 1.2 m/s would need a 16S4P pack (20.5 kWh, +32 kg). At the 1.94 kW shift average, the usable energy lasts about 5.6 h new and 4.5 h at end of life (derived from the table). A 4 h shift, a CC-CV recharge and 0.7 h of transit fit an 8 h slot, so three shifts per day are possible. NASL's figure of about 0.9 ha per day over three shifts corresponds to only about 3 km of cutting per shift at a 1.0 m swath (under an hour at 1.0 m/s), so the 70 % cutting duty of the budget is conservative for the palm farm (spec 2.1).
{tab:tab_pwr_ph1energy} lists the pack consumption measured in two Phase 1 runs.

Battery during the D1 demo drive (2026-10-23 20:11): pack terminal voltage (truth and BMS measurement), pack current (peak 25.5 A in the 10 ms log), SOC (truth and BMS estimate, 95.85 % -> 95.79 %) and the hottest and coldest cell temperatures.

blocks.text: Phase 1 currents stay far below the BMS ratings (at most 26 A against 200 A continuous). With about 6.5 mΩ from the cells to the bus, a 25 A step changes the pack voltage by only about 0.16 V, and a 64 s drive moves the SOC by less than 0.1 %, so the traces in {fig:F30_battery.png} are nearly flat at this scale. The 4 h endurance scenario S3 (new, end-of-life and hot pack) has not yet been run in the full system: it needs about 8 h of wall time in Normal mode. The shift budget is verified on the power benches instead (T-PWR-13 end-of-life endurance, T-PWR-20 24 h shift cycle).
Working with the power model

The following commands open the power models, change their parameters and run the relevant checks. They assume the project is open; `phase1_test_drive` rebuilds `P` from the parameter files at every call, while `run_scenario` uses the base-workspace `P` unless you pass one.

openProject('<project root>\Shaddad_UGV.prj');
open_system('Power_Plant')       % plant, subsystems/power/Power_Plant.slx
open_system('Shaddad_BMS')       % BMS firmware model
open_system('Safety_Chain')      % also PDU, LV_Distribution, Pack_Thermal
P.power.pack                     % pack parameters in the base workspace
edit param_power                 % change a value, then rebuild P, Ts and VC_*:
shaddad_params();
Then run the checks: the power-up scenario, the demonstration drive with the battery signals, the precharge finding with the specification resistor, the lumped pack variant and the power benches:

r0  = run_scenario('S0');        % power-up / re-arm check, 10 s
res = phase1_test_drive();       % D1 demo; battery panel in the result figure
S = res.S;
plot(S.power_truth.SOC_pack_true.t, S.power_truth.SOC_pack_true.v)

P2 = P; P2.sim.ovr.R_pre = 22;  % reproduce the precharge finding with the spec resistor
r22 = run_scenario('S0', 'P', P2);

VC_PACK = 2; r0L = run_scenario('S0'); VC_PACK = 1;   % lumped pack variant

runtests('tests/power/t_power_plant.m');   % T05 benches (about 41 min)
runtests('tests/power/t_pack_bms.m');      % T04 benches; long cases reuse work/T04 caches

items: Logged power signals of a scenario result: `S.power_truth` (true SOC, energies, pack current), `S.power_status` (Safety_OK, Safety_HV_OK, rails), `S.bms_telem` (HV_Ready, SOC estimate, limits, fault words).
Scenario files set the variant controls through `SimulationInput`. Base values such as `VC_PACK` are used unless the scenario overrides them, and the base workspace is not changed.

Individual benches: `pwr_case_run(name)` runs one of the 19 `tb_pack_bms` cases (for example precharge, overcurrent, hppc, capacity, cccv25, hot45, soc_est, balance, eol_mow; `pwr_case_def()` lists them all), and `pp_run('tb_power_plant', TB, ...)` runs the plant bench with a test-bench struct from `tb_power_plant_default`.

blocks.text: To see the safety chain at work without a long run, use `phase1_test_drive('EStopAt', 20, 'ResetAt', 25)`. Note that this is the RC software E-stop. For the hardware loop (front button, STO, 1.5 s delayed K1 opening), run the S8a scenario (`run_scenario('S8a')`) and plot `S.power_status.Safety_OK` and `S.power_status.Safety_HV_OK`.
Verification status and known deviations

The power benches are largely green. `t_power_plant` passes 25 of 26 tests; the only failure is the shift-bench speed target. `t_pack_bms` passes 21 of 27, with one speed failure, four accepted spec deviations and one blocked code-generation test. {tab:tab_pwr_dev} lists the deviations relevant to this chapter.

rows: About 3 % low; energy and V_pack at 50 % pass

Only 22 % of R1 develops in 10 s (τ1 = 40 s). Accepted.

blocks.text: Details of the accepted deviations: in T-PWR-01 the weakest group (seeded capacity deviation) still holds residual SOC when its loaded voltage reaches 2.80 V, and the delivered charge equals that group's capacity x (1 - residual SOC) within 0.5 %; the energy (15.0-15.6 kWh) and V_pack at 50 % SOC (52.0 ± 0.4 V) criteria pass. In T-PWR-02 the measured 10 s resistance agrees with the cell tables within 5 %; the hand calculation of the spec assumed the full R1 after 10 s. In T-PWR-09 (cached bench run `work/T04/cccv25.mat`) the CV overshoot (≤ 15 mV), final SOC (≥ 0.97) and grid energy (≤ 15.8 kWh) criteria pass; the charge only ends earlier, because the 1-RC cell (τ1 = 40 s) tapers from 100 A to 10 A in minutes instead of the 0.5 h CV phase of the hand calculation. The precharge-to-K2 latency is 10 ms BMS output Unit Delay + 10 ms deterministic Rate Transition + 10 ms K2 pickup.

**Side effects of the 4.7 Ω override (hand estimates, not simulated).** With V_pack about 53.6 V: (1) the precharge peak current is about 11 A, above the 10 A class assumed for K2; (2) a precharge into a shorted bus (T-PWR-03b, verified only with 22 Ω and at most 200 J) would dissipate about 0.6 kW in R_pre for the 1.5 s timeout, roughly 0.9 kJ per attempt; (3) with about 14 W of ESC idle load the precharged bus settles near 97.6 % of V_pack, only just above the 0.97 close threshold. Choose the final R_pre together with K2, the resistor energy rating and the close threshold, then re-run T-PWR-03, T-PWR-03b and S0.

Other open points from the spec: where the BMS runs (O1: dedicated STM32G4 board as modelled, the main MCU, or a commercial BMS whose CAN map the model would then mirror); confirmation of the 5.5 mF DC-link capacitance by the drive domain (O2); a safety review of stop category 1 against ISO 18497 / ISO 13849 (O4); and cell hysteresis, which is not modelled, so SOC estimation on a real pack will be worse than in simulation (R4).
